question: Which of the following increased the legal age of marriage for girls from 10 years to 12 years in British India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Age of Consent Bill, 1891**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Age of Consent Bill, 1891 was a legislative act in British India which sought to raise the age of consent for sexual intercourse for girls from 10 to 12 years.
 
• This act was a result of increasing social reform movements and the influence of British administrators who aimed to improve the status of women in Indian society.
 
• The bill was introduced by Sir Andrew Scoble and supported by prominent Indian social reformers such as Behramji Malabari.
 
• The Age of Consent Bill was a significant step towards addressing child marriage and protecting the rights of young girls in British India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindu Widows Remarriage Act of 1856**

 
 
• This act legalized the remarriage of Hindu widows in British India.
 
• It was a major social reform aimed at improving the condition of Hindu widows who were often subjected to harsh treatment and social ostracism.
 
• The act was passed during the tenure of Lord Dalhousie and was supported by social reformers like Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.
 
 
 
• **Pitt's India Act of 1784**
 
 
• This act was passed by the British Parliament to address the governance and control of the East India Company in India.
 
• It established a dual system of control with the British government having the ultimate authority over the company's activities in India.
 
• The act led to the appointment of the Board of Control to supervise the administration of the company in India.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act of 1935**
 
 
• This act was a major legislative reform that aimed to provide greater autonomy to Indian provinces and establish a federal structure.
 
• It introduced provincial autonomy, allowing elected Indian representatives to have more control over local governance.
 
• The act also proposed the creation of an All-India Federation, though this was never fully implemented.
